_why: M4 lab end state, read after "Commit the node layer" and before "Teardown". SIMULATED: the control plane, the kubelet, the DaemonSet rollout and the claim lifecycle are real; every device is a synthetic device published by the upstream example driver. Object state only (D-17, TRUST-06): claim allocation, ResourceSlice, Pod condition, the KEP-4680 health field, the DaemonSet revision and the learner's Grid files. No Pod phase is asserted alone and no number is read as performance. Every kubectl sets KUBECONFIG and --context kind-grid-core itself. Every matches is anchored and in JavaScript regex dialect. The vendor resource name of part 4 appears nowhere in this file (STANDARDS.md C23); the bridge is asserted through the Pod's extendedResourceClaimStatus and the claim it names, and the mock section's device-plugin resource is selected by its /gpu suffix (plan 05-38). Paths are relative to the learner tree (the labs repo root); in src run it from labs/ with: (cd labs && node ../scripts/run-checks.mjs m4/checks.json).

checks.describe: the worker's ResourceSlices report the renamed driver and 8 synthetic devices, read after the sharing part's rollout undo. Printed from a jq fold, so zero slices prints devices=0 and fails
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.spec.nodeName == "grid-core-worker")] | "driver=" + ([.[].spec.driver] | unique | join(",")) + " devices=" + ([.[].spec.devices // [] | length] | add // 0 | tostring)'

checks.describe: part 1: Pod count-over asked for one more course-named extended resource than the node advertised, and its PodScheduled condition says why — read from the condition, never the phase
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-count get pod count-over -o json | jq -r '.status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "PodScheduled") | "status=\(.status) reason=\(.reason) insufficient=" + (((.message // "") | capture("Insufficient (?<r>sim-accelerator\\.example\\.com/device)") | .r) // "none")'

checks.describe: part 2: the holder Pod that kept its device through the broken driver revision and the rollback is the same Pod — its live UID equals the holder-uid-before line the learner recorded
checks.run: sh -c 'live=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-lifecycle get pod holder -o jsonpath="{.metadata.uid}"); before=$(sed -n "s/^holder-uid-before:[[:space:]]*//p" grid-platform/nodes/lifecycle/rollback-record.md 2>/dev/null | head -1); if [ -n "$live" ] && [ "$live" = "$before" ]; then echo uid=unchanged; else echo "uid=changed live=$live before=$before"; fi'

checks.describe: part 2: the holder container never restarted across the driver roll and its undo
checks.run: sh -c 'printf "restarts=%s\n" "$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-lifecycle get pod holder -o jsonpath="{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}")"'

checks.describe: part 2 and part 5: the driver DaemonSet's template is back on the pinned digest, every desired plugin Pod is ready, and its ControllerRevision history holds at least two revisions, which is what a rollout undo reads. A 0/0 DaemonSet cannot satisfy the backreference
checks.run: sh -c 'img=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n dra-example-driver get ds dra-example-driver-kubeletplugin -o jsonpath="{.spec.template.spec.containers[?(@.name==\"plugin\")].image}"); rd=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n dra-example-driver get ds dra-example-driver-kubeletplugin -o jsonpath="{.status.numberReady}/{.status.desiredNumberScheduled}"); rv=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n dra-example-driver get controllerrevisions -o json | jq "[.items[] | select(any(.metadata.ownerReferences[]?; .kind == \"DaemonSet\" and .name == \"dra-example-driver-kubeletplugin\"))] | length"); if [ "$img" = "registry.k8s.io/dra-example-driver/dra-example-driver@sha256:c1488eb51e086bd6b885a667c7d059382844e54e5917a71bcf734c04edfbb62f" ]; then i=pinned; else i="$img"; fi; echo "image=$i ready=$rd revisions=$rv"'

checks.describe: part 2: DeviceTaintRule is served at resource.k8s.io/v1 on this cluster, and the readiness-gate manifest the lab applied is written at that version — never the upstream example's prerelease version
checks.run: sh -c 's=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core api-resources --api-group=resource.k8s.io --no-headers | awk "\$1 == \"devicetaintrules\" { print \$(NF-2) }"); m=$(sed -n "s/^apiVersion:[[:space:]]*//p" m4/readiness-rule.yaml | head -1); echo "served=$s manifest=$m"'

checks.describe: part 3: the claim generated for Pod attr-root-80 is allocated, and the device it was allocated reads pcieRoot pci0000:80 in the ResourceSlice — selection by attribute, not by count
checks.run: sh -c 'export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; c=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get pod attr-root-80 -o jsonpath="{.status.resourceClaimStatuses[0].resourceClaimName}"); d=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get resourceclaim "$c" -o jsonpath="{.status.allocation.devices.results[0].device}" 2>/dev/null); p=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get resourceclaim "$c" -o jsonpath="{.status.allocation.devices.results[0].pool}" 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$d" ] || [ -z "$p" ]; then echo "allocated=no claim=$c"; exit 0; fi; r=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json | jq -r --arg d "$d" --arg p "$p" "[.items[] | select(.spec.pool.name == \$p) | .spec.devices[]? | select(.name == \$d) | .attributes[\"resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot\"].string] | first // \"none\""); echo "allocated=yes pcieRoot=$r"'

checks.describe: part 3: the prioritized-alternatives claim records which subrequest was satisfied, in the <request>/<subrequest> form, and it is the fallback because no device satisfies the preferred selector
checks.run: sh -c 'export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; c=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get pod attr-first-available -o jsonpath="{.status.resourceClaimStatuses[0].resourceClaimName}"); printf "request=%s\n" "$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get resourceclaim "$c" -o jsonpath="{.status.allocation.devices.results[0].request}" 2>/dev/null)"'

checks.describe: part 3, the deliberate failure: claim sim-device-100gi exists with no allocation, and its Pod's PodScheduled condition is False. The claim's own name is printed first, so an absent claim cannot read as unallocated
checks.run: sh -c 'a=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get resourceclaim sim-device-100gi -o jsonpath="{.metadata.name}/{.status.allocation.devices.results[0].device}" 2>/dev/null); if [ "$a" = "sim-device-100gi/" ]; then al=none; else al="unexpected:$a"; fi; s=$(KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-attr get pod attr-unsatisfiable -o jsonpath="{.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"PodScheduled\")].status}"); echo "allocation=$al scheduled=$s"'

checks.describe: part 4: Pod unchanged-manifest carries no resourceClaims in its spec, yet the scheduler created a claim for it, named in status.extendedResourceClaimStatus, and that claim is allocated. The resource name itself is never read here
checks.run: sh -c 'export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; n=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-bridge get pod unchanged-manifest -o json | jq "(.spec.resourceClaims // []) | length"); c=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-bridge get pod unchanged-manifest -o jsonpath="{.status.extendedResourceClaimStatus.resourceClaimName}"); if [ -n "$c" ] && kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-bridge get resourceclaim "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then cl=created; else cl=none; fi; d=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-bridge get resourceclaim "$c" -o jsonpath="{.status.allocation.devices.results[0].device}" 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$d" ]; then al=yes; else al=no; fi; echo "spec-claims=$n claim=$cl allocated=$al"'

checks.describe: part 5: one ResourceClaim, shared-claim, is reserved for both shared-a and shared-b, and both containers started with the claim's allocated device injected, read from inside each Pod. Run 1 showed reservedFor listing two Pods whose containers never started, so reservedFor alone could not fail on that state. Two Pods on one allocated device is DRA-native sharing and demonstrates no isolation
checks.run: sh -c 'export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; r=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-sharing get resourceclaim shared-claim -o json | jq "[.status.reservedFor[]? | select(.name == \"shared-a\" or .name == \"shared-b\")] | length"); d=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-sharing get resourceclaim shared-claim -o jsonpath="{.status.allocation.devices.results[0].device}"); a=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-sharing exec shared-a -- sh -c env 2>/dev/null | sed -n "s/^GPU_DEVICE_[0-9][0-9]*=//p"); b=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-sharing exec shared-b -- sh -c env 2>/dev/null | sed -n "s/^GPU_DEVICE_[0-9][0-9]*=//p"); if [ -n "$d" ] && [ "$a" = "$d" ] && [ "$b" = "$d" ]; then s=yes; else s=no; fi; echo "reservedFor=$r same-device=$s"'

checks.describe: part 6: after the health probe drove a device Unhealthy and back, Pod health-watch's own KEP-4680 field reports Healthy — object state, never a phase
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-health get pod health-watch -o json | jq -r '"health=" + ([.status.containerStatuses[]?.allocatedResourcesStatus[]?.resources[]?.health] | unique | join(","))'

checks.describe: the mock section, part one: the worker's allocatable carries exactly one resource whose name ends in /gpu, advertised by the vendor's unmodified device plugin from the mock's devices, and it is non-zero. The resource is selected by its suffix and never spelled (STANDARDS.md C23 clause 8); the count is a profile constant, not a reading, so only non-zero is asserted. A teardown leaves the key with allocatable 0 (plan 05-37), which fails here
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core get node grid-core-worker -o json | jq -r '[.status.allocatable // {} | to_entries[] | select(.key | endswith("/gpu"))] | "suffix_resources=" + (length | tostring) + " allocatable_nonzero=" + ([.[] | .value | tonumber | select(. > 0)] | length | tostring)'

checks.describe: the mock section, part one: Pod mock-plugin-one asks for one unit of a resource whose name ends in /gpu, its PodScheduled condition is True, and its container carries the mock's own MOCK_NVML_CONFIG variable, read from inside the Pod. That variable is what says the container's view of the hardware is the mock's injection, not a driver's. Object state, never the phase
checks.run: sh -c 'export KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}"; s=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-mock get pod mock-plugin-one -o jsonpath="{.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"PodScheduled\")].status}"); r=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-mock get pod mock-plugin-one -o json | jq "[.spec.containers[].resources.limits // {} | keys[] | select(endswith(\"/gpu\"))] | length"); e=$(kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-mock exec mock-plugin-one -- sh -c env 2>/dev/null | grep -c "^MOCK_NVML_CONFIG="); echo "scheduled=$s requests_suffix=$r mock_env=$e"'

checks.describe: the mock section's deliberate failure: Pod mock-plugin-over asked for one more than the device plugin advertised, and its PodScheduled condition is False, Unschedulable, naming an Insufficient resource whose name ends in /gpu — read from the condition, never the phase, and the resource never spelled
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n m4-mock get pod mock-plugin-over -o json | jq -r '.status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "PodScheduled") | "status=\(.status) reason=\(.reason) insufficient=" + (((.message // "") | capture("Insufficient [a-z0-9.-]+(?<r>/gpu)(,| |$)") | .r) // "none")'

checks.describe: part 2's record in the learner's repository: all ten keys present, the holder UIDs are UUID-form and equal, and both plugin Pod UIDs recorded
checks.run: sh -c 'f=grid-platform/nodes/lifecycle/rollback-record.md; n=0; for k in holder-uid-before holder-uid-after holder-restarts-before holder-restarts-after holder-device-before holder-device-after plugin-pod-uid-before plugin-pod-uid-after slice-generation-before slice-generation-after; do c=$(grep -c "^$k:" "$f" 2>/dev/null); [ "$c" = "1" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; hb=$(sed -n "s/^holder-uid-before:[[:space:]]*//p" "$f" 2>/dev/null | head -1); ha=$(sed -n "s/^holder-uid-after:[[:space:]]*//p" "$f" 2>/dev/null | head -1); pb=$(sed -n "s/^plugin-pod-uid-before:[[:space:]]*//p" "$f" 2>/dev/null | head -1); pa=$(sed -n "s/^plugin-pod-uid-after:[[:space:]]*//p" "$f" 2>/dev/null | head -1); u=$(printf "%s\n" "$hb" | grep -cx "[0-9a-f]\{8\}-[0-9a-f]\{4\}-[0-9a-f]\{4\}-[0-9a-f]\{4\}-[0-9a-f]\{12\}"); h=differ; if [ "$u" = "1" ] && [ "$hb" = "$ha" ]; then h=equal; fi; p=missing; if [ -n "$pb" ] && [ -n "$pa" ]; then p=recorded; fi; echo "keys=$n holder=$h plugin=$p"'

checks.describe: part 6's classification in the learner's repository: under the fixed header, one row each for XID 48, 63 and 79, every cell non-empty. Kept, with its run unchanged, because the published grid-v0.5 capability row cites it (STANDARDS.md C20) and it reads the rows only, whatever the evidence source; xid-classification-cites-live-exporter is the entry that fails on a fixture-era source (plan 05-38)
checks.run: awk -F'|' 'BEGIN { h = 0; n = 0; x = "" } /^\| XID \| Evidence \| Class \| First action \|/ { h = 1; next } h && /^\|[[:space:]]*(48|63|79)[[:space:]]*\|/ { ok = (NF >= 6); for (i = 2; i <= 5; i++) { c = $i; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", c); if (c == "") ok = 0 } if (ok) { id = $2; gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", id); n++; x = x (x == "" ? "" : ",") id } } END { print "rows=" n " xids=" x }' grid-platform/nodes/health/xid-classification.md

checks.describe: the mock section's classification in the learner's repository: under the fixed header, one row each for XID 48, 63 and 79, every cell non-empty, and an evidence-source line that cites the live dcgm-exporter reading mock devices. Replaces the fixture-era entry, whose source was the course-authored file alone (D-60 supersedes D-15 step 6)
checks.run: awk -F'|' 'BEGIN { h = 0; n = 0; x = "" } /^\| XID \| Evidence \| Class \| First action \|/ { h = 1; next } h && /^\|[[:space:]]*(48|63|79)[[:space:]]*\|/ { ok = (NF >= 6); for (i = 2; i <= 5; i++) { c = $i; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", c); if (c == "") ok = 0 } if (ok) { id = $2; gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", id); n++; x = x (x == "" ? "" : ",") id } } END { print "rows=" n " xids=" x }' grid-platform/nodes/health/xid-classification.md; printf 'source_live_exporter=%s\n' "$(grep -c '^Evidence source: the live dcgm-exporter.*mock devices' grid-platform/nodes/health/xid-classification.md 2>/dev/null)"

checks.describe: the three addon-dra wrappers in the learner's repository, with comment lines stripped, each exec the single-source addon script of the same name — wrappers, not copies, so the driver pin has one authority
checks.run: sh -c 'o=""; for n in create verify teardown; do c=$(grep -v "^[[:space:]]*#" "grid-platform/clusters/addon-dra/$n.sh" 2>/dev/null | grep -F "/clusters/grid-core/addons/dra/$n.sh" | grep -c "^exec "); if [ "$c" = "1" ]; then s=exec; else s=missing; fi; o="$o $n=$s"; done; echo "${o# }"'
